newsitem.title: KUWAIT: U.S. troops pound "enemies" in Kuwaiti desert.
newsitem.headline: U.S. troops pound "enemies" in Kuwaiti desert.

text.p: U.S. troops pumped artillery shells at imaginary enemies in the Kuwaiti desert on Friday in a signal to Iraq that Washington was determined to defend its oil-rich Gulf allies.

U.S. Army First Cavalry Division gunners and support crews taking part in long-scheduled exercises said they were ready to start shooting for real if the latest war of words between Baghdad and Washington turned into a military confrontation.

"If we are called on to assume a more serious mission then yes, we are ready," said Sergeant Michal Borelli amid billowing dust on a windy, scorching late summer day at a training range about 40 km (25 miles) from the Iraqi border.
"We are training everyday in case that (military action) comes around the corner. We are ready for it."

The air shook to the roar of track-propelled Paladin M109A6 Howitzer artillery guns. Heavy machineguns mounted on Humvee general purpose vehicles made a deafening rattle as gunners shredded targets that popped up out of the desert floor.

A U.S. military statement said the live fire exercise, the latest in a five-year-old series called Intrinsic Action, involved 1,100 troops. The exercise was aimed at improving readiness between Kuwaiti and U.S. forces and strengthening the ability of the U.S. military to deploy quickly in the region.

Iraq, in a fresh standoff with Washington over the expansion of a southern no-fly zone, told Kuwait on Thursday it would be committing an act of war if it allowed U.S. Stealth warplanes to use its territory for attacks on his country.
The U.S. jets were moving into position for possible bombing raids against Iraq after Iraqi forces fired a surface-to-air missile at U.S. fighters over northern Iraq on Wednesday.

The Pentagon said Iraqi forces fired three anti-aircraft missiles into the air over southern Iraq on Thursday, but added that the missiles were apparently fired blindly and came nowhere near U.S. and allied warplanes.
The men from Task Force 1/9, First Cavalry Division, deployed to Kuwait on August 10 for about 120 days of exercises, drawing weaponry pre-positioned in Kuwait.

Private first class Allan Goodwin, referring to U.S. cruise missiles attacks on Iraq last week, said: "I think with the cruise missile attacks the danger level has gone up quite a bit here in Kuwait. But I don't foresee us going to war with Iraq."
"I'd rather be elsewhere. But as long as I'm here I'll do the best job I can," he said.
Paladin driver specialist Daniel Moore said: "I feel this whole battery is ready. We do the job that has to be done."
